notes: Quiet day. Ran a four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents, ~150 queries total, every lane hitting EGRESS_BLOCKED on direct WebFetch to vendor domains and falling back to WebSearch (mentioned once here per the rules, not filed per-URL). No lane found a genuine new same-day (Oct 25/26) announcement: the AI lane's candidates (xAI grok-imagine-image-quality retirement, OpenAI GPT-5/o3 snapshot removal, OpenAI fine-tuning/audio retirements, NVIDIA GTC 2027, ICLR 2027, Geneva AI Summit 2027) were all cross-checked and are already on file, several in already-flagged duplicate clusters. The devtools/cloud lane independently re-derived a cluster of AWS/Azure/GitHub/database lifecycle dates (GHES 3.20 EOL, AWS Service Management Connector EOS, Azure Front Door classic retirement, AWS Lambda Node 22 deprecation, Elasticsearch 8.19 EOL, MongoDB 7.0 EOL, GitHub Universe 2026, AWS re:Invent 2026) that turned out to already be on file essentially verbatim at matching or better confidence — none re-filed. The security lane's one forward-looking candidate (CA/Browser Forum 100-day cert cap, 2027-03-15) is the same fact already on file four times over (see concerns); its second candidate (Chrome Root Program removing the client-auth EKU from public certs) was left unfiled because vendor sources disagree on the exact day (Feb 1 vs Mar 1 vs Mar 15, 2027) and none of them is Google's own policy page — worth a follow-up once a primary source is reachable. The bigtech/hardware/mobile lane's only new find, Telstra's Nov 16, 2026 Android RCS rollout in Australia, was left unfiled as a single-carrier, single-country feature rollout rather than a platform-level mobile event. Two EU AI Act Digital Omnibus deadlines (Annex III high-risk compliance pushed to 2027-12-02, Annex I to 2028-08-02) are both beyond the 12-month window from today and were left out per the rules rather than filed and immediately pruned. What this run did file: three Anthropic model minimum-guaranteed-support-floor dates (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8) that the 2026-10-25 run log identified and sourced from Anthropic's own model-deprecations page but dropped because a dry run showed them incorrectly collapsing into the existing Claude Opus 4.6 entry. This run tracked the collapse down to a second, more specific failure mode than the one already flagged (see concerns) and verified dedupe-safe titles for all three via --dry-run before filing.
concerns: Found the specific mechanism behind the Claude model-support-floor merge bug flagged in the 2026-10-25 run log, and it is not just the EVENT_DRIFT_DAYS/token-weighting issue already described there: src/lib/id.ts's tokens() helper calls slugify(), which silently slice(0,60)s the ENTIRE title string before splitting it into words — so any title whose slugified form runs past 60 characters loses its tail, and if that tail is the one word or digit that distinguishes it from a similar existing title (e.g. 'Anthropic ends minimum guaranteed support for Claude Opus 4.7' slugifies to 61 chars and the truncation drops the trailing '-7', leaving only 'claude opus 4' where '4.7' should disambiguate from 'Claude Opus 4.6'), sameTitle() then compares against a title that has effectively lost its own identity. Verified with npx tsx scripts/apply-findings.ts --dry-run: that exact phrasing collapsed into the existing anthropic-claude-opus-4-6-reaches-minimum-guaranteed-support-2027-02 entry and overwrote its date; a shorter rephrasing ('Claude Opus 4.7 drops out of guaranteed support', 49 chars after slugification) filed as a separate, correct entry instead. This run worked around it by keeping all three new Anthropic titles short enough to stay under the 60-char slug limit, confirmed via --dry-run before filing for real. A maintainer fix should either stop truncating inside tokens() (only deriveId needs the length cap, for URL/filename friendliness) or truncate after tokenizing rather than before.

The CA/Browser Forum 100-day public TLS certificate validity cap (2027-03-15) now has a fourth near-duplicate row on file (data/events/2027-03.json: 'CA/Browser Forum cuts max public TLS certificate validity to 100 days', 'CA/Browser Forum cuts max TLS certificate life to 100 days', 'CA/Browser Forum TLS certificate max validity drops to 100 days', 'TLS certificate rules tighten: 100-day validity and serverAuth-only EKU') — all correctly dated, all independently re-found by this run's security lane, none re-filed to avoid a fifth. This is the same src/lib/id.ts sameTitle/sameOrg limitation flagged in prior run logs (2026-10-23, 2026-10-24, 2026-10-25); still needs a maintainer merge of the four rows plus the underlying fix.
